title: The Canopy Pulse Underground

features.name: root-signal-junction
features.desc-on-touch: The pulse bifurcates: where electrical impulse becomes nutrient surge. You feel it moving both down and up at once, unable to distinguish sender from receiver.

features.name: mycelial-broadcast
features.desc-on-touch: Thread-thin filaments spread through dark soil, each one carrying packets of light that should not exist in soil. The archive is learning to root.

features.name: antenna-in-earth
features.desc-on-touch: The transceiver rod has bent—or grown—into the humus. Its LED still blinks. The distinction between hardware and decay has become unclear.

features.name: cross-section-teaching
features.desc-on-touch: A diagram that was never drawn: layers of bark, circuit board, root mat, wire, soil. The archive is rendering its own cross-section.

features.name: pulse-chamber
features.desc-on-touch: A space beneath the soil where two kinds of rhythm learned to synchronize. You can hear them separately if you listen hard; together, they sound like a single breath.

inscription: where the circuit goes down to learn what root systems already know
